_readme: English datasheet-header -> field_key map, for the WP3 deep extractor.
Separate from attribute-aliases.de.json because that one maps HexCat's authored GERMAN
attribute names; this one maps Cisco's own English table labels.
Rules are ORDERED REGEXES matched CASE-INSENSITIVELY, because the same fact is worded
differently across datasheet generations and even within one sheet:
'Product Description' / 'Product description' / '[Product description]'
'MTBF hours' / 'MTBF Hours' / 'MTBF (hours)' / 'Mean time between failures (hours)'
'Power consumption (worst case)' / 'Power consumption (W) (no more than)' /
'Power Consumption (Watts) (No More Than)'
First match wins, so specific patterns come first: 'Switching capacity with stacking' must
be matched before 'Switching capacity'.
Sentinels:
__not_a_spec     : ordering/marketing/licensing metadata that must never enter specs_v2
__compat         : a real fact that belongs in the COMPAT store, not a spec field
('Supported SFP modules' - 1,302 rows across the 10 golden sheets)
__duplicate_unit : the same fact in a second unit (inches beside centimetres, pounds
beside kilograms). Dropped so completeness is not double counted.
__backlog        : a real spec with no field_key yet; a NAMED gap, reported not guessed.
AXIS ORDER: dimension labels are not consistently H x W x D. The 3850/3650 sheets use
'Unit dimensions (W x D x H)'. map-deep-specs.ts reads the axis order out of the label and
reorders the parsed triple; storing it positionally would silently file width as height.

Two corrections after reading real values [M 2026-09-01]: 'Default AC power supply' yields '715W AC' (a rating) and was mapped to the psu_config ENUM, producing ENUM_VIOLATION on every row; it now feeds psu_options. 'Network module' yields 'C3850-NM-4-1G, C3850-NM-2-10G, ...' (a module list) and was mapped to the numeric module_slots, producing RANGE_VIOLATION; it is now __compat. Both were the mapping being wrong, not the data.
THREE FIELDS PULLED BACK TO __backlog 2026-09-01 after checking column semantics by hand.
The provenance audit passed 10,493/10,493 - every value really was in the cell we recorded - but
passing that says nothing about whether the LABEL over the cell means what we assumed. Two of
these tables are keyed by a configuration (which PSU, which input voltage, half vs full port
traffic) that the schema has nowhere to record, so 'first row wins' silently picked one.
Better to hold the field than to publish a number that is right for a configuration nobody asked about.
